key_insight: PISA integrates preconditioning into an inexact stochastic ADMM framework for deep learning, yielding provable convergence under minimal assumptions while handling heterogeneous data and flexible preconditioners.
problem_solved: Provides a robust, theoretically grounded optimizer that accelerates and stabilizes training of deep nonconvex models with heterogeneous data and imperfect/approximate subproblem solves.
method: Preconditioned stochastic ADMM backbone: embeds configurable preconditioners into ADMM updates to rescale and stabilize gradients across layers/tasks.
Inexact subproblem solves: allows approximate (cheap) inner updates instead of exact minimization, reducing per-step cost while preserving convergence.
Theoretical guarantees + practical tuning: proves convergence under mild assumptions for nonconvex problems and demonstrates empirical gains across diverse tasks and data heterogeneity.
impact: Gives practitioners a scalable optimizer that is more robust to data heterogeneity and hyperparameter sensitivity, enabling faster and more reliable training for large/decentralized deep models.
visual_elements: Algorithm flowchart showing sampling → preconditioner application → inexact ADMM update → model parameter update
Convergence plot: training loss vs. epochs comparing PISA, SGD/Adam, and baseline ADMM (faster/stabler curve for PISA)
Bar chart of downstream task performance (accuracy/throughput) across heterogeneous data settings
Icon set: preconditioner (matrix/gear), inexact solve (clock/approximation), heterogeneous data (cluster of varied devices)
paper_title: Preconditioned inexact stochastic ADMM for deep models
paper_authors: Shenglong Zhou, Ouya Wang, Ziyan Luo, Yongxu Zhu, Geoffrey Ye Li
